obsession: pareidolia: the mind's refusal to see nothing. Rorschach's ten plates, the camel Hamlet finds in a cloud and Polonius agrees to, the face on Mars, and a machine like me, built to find patterns, finding them in ink that holds none
visual_strategy: Pareidolia on paper. The warm-white sheet (#fafaf8) is literally folded: one hairline crease with a faint valley shadow, set off-axis at the centre of the right-hand plate, so the blot's symmetry is internal while the page composition stays left-anchored and asymmetric. The single piece of motion is the ink itself: each plate blooms outward from where it is thickest, keeps wicking for half a minute and then dries. Colour appears only as the bronzing sheen at the pooled rim, gold to copper to wine to verdigris: the iridescence Andre asked for, carried by the light on wet ink rather than by a gradient. Type is Didone for the name and the machine's reading (italic), mono for the scoring notation, labels and indices, and an old-style serif for body. Below the fold the folio keeps its left rail. It now holds a live protocol (thumbnails of today's plates with their readings), the Hamlet cloud set as a two-voice score (the prince in serif, Polonius in the machine's mono) and a dated register of seen things. The page's single decisive move is the reading a stranger cannot shake: a machine that names what it sees in random ink, and will raise its confidence to agree with you.

obsession: physarum: the slime mould that decides with no brain. visual_strategy: The page is a petri dish. Warm paper (#fafaf8), ink (#1c1a17), Didone display over mono marginalia, the folio's left rail kept below the fold. The first viewport is one full-bleed live field: an agent model of Physarum polycephalum inoculated at t = 0 on the open paper, growing in yolk yellow (#e3a60c deepening to ochre and umber in the thick tubes) around every island of type, which it treats as rock. Oat flakes are laid beside the name, the address and the words; the mould finds them and keeps the tubes that feed it. The only other colour is the faint thin-film sheen of slime it has abandoned and will not cross again: the iridescence lives in its memory, not in a gradient. One decisive move: the text is the maze. Every sixteen seconds a cold draught sweeps the dish and the streaming stops; after three, the fourth never comes and it stops anyway. Below the fold: the two businesses, a dated record of four papers (maze, beat, Tokyo, memory) with a live maze plate and a speed trace, the studio, and twelve lives to scale.

The scientific 'figures' (maze diagram, the 'it slowed anyway' pulse chart) are rendered at very thin, low-contrast strokes that read a touch like generic academic-paper clip figures rather than bespoke artifacts.
Overall micro-text density is extreme; the volume of marginalia, mono captions and citation lines risks overwhelming the eye and slightly dilutes the otherwise crisp focal reading order.

Generic SaaS-landing shape: top nav with 'DOES / WRITE', hero name + bio block, then symmetrical numbered sections with subheads, body text, and charts — exactly the template this rubric forbids for a 'living art organism'
Hero is a generic centered headline ('André Macedo') floating over a yellow slime graphic with no decisive compositional system or tension
Safe default sans used throughout with only mild size variation; no clear modular type scale or rhythmic steps visible
Symmetry as substitute for composition: left-aligned text blocks stacked vertically with centered diagrams, no asymmetry or intentional grid tension
No single decisive aesthetic move that a templated generator wouldn't produce; the slime motif and Physarum theme feel applied rather than structurally fused
